title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Amount of the Returned-Payment Fee
content:
On Benefit Overpayment Accounts, the return being charged is the most recent return entry booked on the overpayment, and the repayment returned is identified by the confirmation number on that entry. The returned-payment fee booked for a return is the classification's returned-payment fee, rounded to the cent.

## Reading the ledger

| Item | Where it is read |
|---|---|
| The return being charged | The return entry with the latest booking date on the overpayment's ledger |
| The repayment returned | The confirmation number shown on that return entry |
| The date of the return | The booking date of that return entry |
| The classification's returned-payment fee | The returned-payment fee figure listed for the overpayment's classification in the Department's payment terms for Benefit Overpayment Accounts |

## Worked example (hypothetical)

An overpayment's ledger shows two return entries: one booked on 3 February for confirmation number LKP-CK-11, and one booked on 18 April for confirmation number LKP-ACH-52.

1. The most recent return entry is the one booked on 18 April, so the return being charged is the return of the repayment with confirmation number LKP-ACH-52.
2. The fee booked for that return is the returned-payment fee listed for the overpayment's classification, rounded to the cent. With a hypothetical listed figure of USD 19.999 the fee would be USD 20.00; a listed figure already in whole cents is booked as it stands.
